notes.summary: Round 3 adds ONE physical knob, CategoryProfile.wheelie_margin: the share of the combined bike + rider wheelie ceiling the rider holds from rest to the 60-ft line (motoquant/physics.py run loop, mirrored in rust/motoquant-core, resolved-config schema 5; 1.0 = bit-identical no-op, verified against a worktree of 1c487f0 on the references + 5 catalog bikes and on the full round-2 report re-measure). Every cluster was re-selected from NEUTRAL over mu_peak_scale 0.97-1.10 x wheelie_margin 0.65-1.00 with launch_rpm_factor retired as a bias corrector (it survives only in the 'margin+lr' family under the 1-SE rule and in the gate escape), joint objective w|d|_ET + 0.01 x w|d|_trap, per-row timing, grouped 5-fold CV, 1-SE rule, and a selection gate = HARD dry-mass monotonicity (zero tolerance) + rider-mass and sea-level probes (inversions only below 10 ms). SHIPPED (all gates honoured): (c) 0.2980 vs 0.2629 (FAIL), bias +0.025, trap bias +3.07 km/h, top speed mean|d| 12.9 km/h, zero dry-mass inversions, zero rider-mass inversions, sea level: HP4 Race 12.0 ms (physics-level, 16.9 ms at neutral, no knob point clears it) + 1199 Panigale 3.7 ms + KTM 1290 SAR 1.2 ms (sea level + rider). The mechanism itself works: the unconstrained CV choices score (c) 0.2570 / bias +0.002 (alt_unconstrained) — the gap to the shipped set is entirely the mass gate on three clusters.

design_decision_window.rejected: all of 1st gear (clutch slip + locked 1st): measured first. At the ET-centring uniform margin (0.80) it leaves the K5 60 ft at 1.80 s from the beam (magazines ~1.9 s) and spends the rest of the ET offset between 60 ft and the 1-2 shift (140-180 km/h on a litre bike), making the pass nearly mass-INSENSITIVE: 37 dry-mass inversions on the 202 litre / sport-twin catalog bikes at margin 0.72, vs 3 (the neutral-physics HP4 / 1199 / V4R) with the 60-ft window. Clutch-slip-only is the same thing here (the slip phase lasts to 108-146 km/h on litre bikes).
design_decision_window.whenever_the_cap_binds: rejected a priori: changes power-limited 2nd/3rd-gear running (trap / top speed) and lengthens the mass-insensitive capped phase

why_et_is_not_met_with_all_gates: litre_sport_195p: the CV choice margin 0.69 (cluster w|d| 0.17) leaves the BMW HP4 Race (-10 kg 9.8 ms slower) and Panigale V4R (2.5 ms) dry-mass inverted. The HP4 inverts at NEUTRAL: 215 hp on 146 kg is wheelie-limited in 1st AND 2nd gear when lighter, and dry mass sits at the bike CoG height, so a heavier bike has a lower system CoG and a higher wheelie ceiling (genuine ballast physics). The only dry-feasible points of the whole grip x margin x launch-rpm box (62 of 6084) are clutch dumps at 0.45-0.475 x redline with grip 1.03-1.05, which make the cluster slow and scattered: cluster w|d| 0.44, CV J 0.56 vs 0.25. Alone this costs (c) ~0.034 (alt_litre195_margin: 0.2639, within +0.005 of 0.2629, but 2 dry inversions).

other: the CV choice margin 0.76 is dry-monotone but leaves rider-mass inversions of 66 ms (Ninja H2 SX SE+) and 18 ms (KTM 1290 Super Adventure R, which inverts at neutral too): both 2nd-gear traction-limited, where a heavier rider loads the rear tyre. The rider-gate-feasible choice (margin 0.66) moves the cluster bias to +0.15.

sport_twin_600_1300: the 1199 Panigale inverts at neutral (traction-limited in 1st/2nd); the gate-feasible 'margin+lr' point (0.75 / 0.50) costs little (cluster w|d| 0.21 vs 0.21 unconstrained on (a)).
two_stroke on (c): margin 0.66 fitted on the round-2 labels is +0.70 s slow on HEAD's 2T labels (w 5.3) — the round-2 data corrections moved those rows; (a) 0.34 / +0.26.
